# Ringshadow

> Ringshadow is an open-source real-time strategy game for the Mac, built in Unreal Engine 5 by one developer and AI coding agents, and dedicated to the public domain (CC0). An AI commander runs your army and you can take over any unit and play it like a shooter. Alongside it an MMORPG mode is being built: you are one Prospector in a lasting world under a ringed gas giant.

Every page below has a Markdown copy at its own address with `.md` added. The source code, art and docs are at https://github.com/ValiDraganescu/ringshadow. The blog's Atom feed is https://ringshadow.com/blog/feed.xml, and everything on this site in one file is https://ringshadow.com/llms-full.txt.

## Pages

- [Ringshadow](https://ringshadow.com/index.md): Ringshadow: a free real-time strategy game for Mac, Windows and Linux. Your AI commander runs the army, and you can dive into any unit and play it like a shooter. Built in public with AI agents, public domain (CC0).
- [The ring of Ringshadow](https://ringshadow.com/roadmap.md): The Ringshadow roadmap: what is done, what comes next and what comes later, from the strategy game to the MMORPG mode.
- [The Ringshadow blog](https://ringshadow.com/blog/index.md): The Ringshadow blog: how the game is being built, as it happens, with albums of pictures from the agents' runs.

## Blog posts (newest first)

- [The Fork: the first canyon to hold](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-fork.md): The first canyon in Ringshadow's world: The Fork in Cold Fork, two winding arms from Brood tunnels to a prize of 36,000 ore and 6,000 MH, with 12 build spots on the rims for the turrets that will hold it.
- [Valleys, not tiles: the regions reshaped](https://ringshadow.com/blog/valleys.md): Ringshadow's nine regions reshaped as natural basins: bays, rock spurs, necks, islands of rock, terraced walls and passages that narrow like canyon mouths, with one high land of rock running between them.
- [A quieter HUD: the same moments, before and after](https://ringshadow.com/blog/hud.md): Ringshadow's HUD, decluttered: one lane of toasts at the upper left, one banner slot under the compass, a contract panel a third of its old height, and the same moments before and after.
- [“I reached level 10, now what?”](https://ringshadow.com/blog/now-what.md): After the first ten minutes, KSTR now keeps one goal in front of every Ringshadow pilot, from a chain of 15 picked by level and by what the pilot has done, from pumping MH at level 3 to the Matriarch at 35.
- [The Brood, painted: before and after the art pass](https://ringshadow.com/blog/brood-art.md): The art pass on Ringshadow's Brood: veined egg shells lit from within, opal chitin that shifts colour with the view, glass wings, the Matriarch's glowing sac and crown, and the gatling gun painted from its forge concept. Before and after.
- [Through the walls: walking between regions](https://ringshadow.com/blog/passages.md): Ringshadow's regions now have grounds of their own, cliff walls and 14 passages between them, and walking from one region into the next happens without a reload or a jump.
- [The world map: the real ground, seen from above](https://ringshadow.com/blog/world-map.md): Press M and Ringshadow's world map shows every region you've been to as a picture of its real ground from above, with live pilots, mercenaries, the Brood, buildings and deposits, and a tooltip on each.
- [The Matriarch wakes in Slag Pockets](https://ringshadow.com/blog/matriarch.md): The Brood's queen now lives at her nest in Slag Pockets: 6,000 hp, a slam, an acid spit and a roar that rallies her horde. Pilots who bring her down share 3,000 ore, 1,500 MH and a rare blueprint.
- [Guns for the realm: the Citadel shoots back](https://ringshadow.com/blog/turrets.md): The Citadel now shoots back with four corner turrets, pilots build a Sentinel AA tower and a gatling gun firing red-hot ore-and-MH rounds, and every placed turret takes upgrades paid from your own wallet.
- [Mercenaries: they mine while you sleep](https://ringshadow.com/blog/mercenaries.md): Hire mercenary prospectors at Ringshadow's Citadel: in a world day each one mines what you mine in an hour, and they keep working while the game is closed.
- [The world runs on after you quit](https://ringshadow.com/blog/world-runs-on.md): Quit Ringshadow and its world keeps going: the local server stays up on the Mac, the clock turns, meteors fall and the Brood roams, at about 0.008% of a CPU core.
- [Coming next: guns for the realm, and a canyon to hold](https://ringshadow.com/blog/defences.md): What is being built now in Ringshadow: the Citadel's guns, an AA tower, a gatling gun firing red-hot ore-and-MH rounds, and a canyon the pilots defend wave by wave.
- [The Brood: from a painting to the world in a day](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-brood.md): Ringshadow's first enemies: four alien bugs, from concept paintings to blockout models to the world, where they linger at deposits, bite, dive, eat ore and raid buildings.
- [Missions, the Journal and three voices](https://ringshadow.com/blog/missions.md): Ringshadow's Citadel now offers missions in three tiers, a Journal keeps them, and three narrators read every briefing: the mission officer, the Warden and a frightened radio dispatcher.
- [The realm: shared buildings, a tax and a shop](https://ringshadow.com/blog/the-realm.md): Ringshadow's buildings now belong to the realm: every pilot uses them, the Citadel takes 10% of every unload, and its shop sells blueprints and supplies.
- [How we got here](https://ringshadow.com/blog/how-we-got-here.md): Two days of building Ringshadow's MMORPG mode: our own server, a world that lasts, a hundred levels, the ringshadow sweep and starfall.
